options.radiante.title: Radiante Settings...
CPU threads that turn chunks into ray tracing geometry. More loads new areas faster when you fly or teleport, but competes with the game for CPU. Lower it if the game stutters; raise it if chunks pop in slowly.
options.radiante.chunk_building_batch_si: How many chunk sections are sent to the GPU in one acceleration structure build. Higher fills the world in faster but can cause frame time spikes while loading; lower is smoother but slower to catch up.
options.radiante.chunk_building_total_ba: How many of those builds may be in flight on the GPU at once. Higher loads faster on strong GPUs and uses more video memory; lower if you see hitches or run out of VRAM.
Blocks that give off light (torches, lava, glowstone) light up the world around them. Off saves some performance but light sources only glow themselves.
options.radiante.biome_ambiance_strength: How thick each biome's haze is. 100% is the tuned, subtle look; lower for clearer long views, higher for more atmosphere. No effect on performance.
options.radiante.cloud_mode.tooltip: How clouds are drawn. Volumetric are real 3D clouds that cast shadows and cost the most; vanilla-style are cheaper; off is fastest.
options.radiante.dlss_mode.tooltip: Internal resolution DLSS renders at before upscaling. Quality looks sharpest and costs the most; Performance and Ultra Performance run faster but look softer and thicken thin details. Custom lets you set the resolution yourself.
options.radiante.ray_reconstruction.tool: Recommended on NVIDIA RTX GPUs. DLSS's own AI denoiser: sharper reflections and fewer smears than NRD. Off, the NRD denoiser cleans the picture and DLSS only upscales it, which can help on weaker GPUs or if Ray Reconstruction smears or ghosts.
options.radiante.frame_generation.toolti: Generates extra frames between rendered ones with %s. Smoother motion on a high refresh monitor, at the cost of a little input latency. A present thread spreads the frames out; V-Sync stays your choice. Not available with HDR output.
message.radiante.ray_tracing_unavailable: Ray tracing is not available on this system
options.radiante.unavailable.hardware: Radiante needs a GPU with hardware ray tracing (VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline). Your graphics card or driver does not report support for it.
options.radiante.unavailable.opengl: Radiante is unavailable because the game is running on OpenGL. Ray tracing needs the Vulkan renderer: set Graphics API to Prefer Vulkan or Default above, then restart the game.
screen.radiante.unsupported.title: Radiante: ray tracing unavailable
screen.radiante.unsupported.message:
Radiante could not start on this system. It needs a graphics card with hardware ray tracing support (VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline), and yours does not report it.

The game keeps running with Minecraft's own renderer. You can carry on as you are, or switch the game to OpenGL - ray tracing is not available there either.
screen.radiante.opengl.title: Switched to OpenGL
screen.radiante.opengl.message:
The game will use OpenGL the next time it starts.

Ray tracing is not available on OpenGL, so Radiante's settings will stay closed. To come back, set useOpenGl=false in radiante/options.properties.
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.open:
The game is running on OpenGL, and ray tracing does not exist on that graphics API, so Radiante stays off and its settings stay closed.

Switch the game to Vulkan and restart to use Radiante.
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.fail:
The last start of Minecraft did not finish - it crashed, or another Minecraft was opening at the same time - so this session started on OpenGL to be safe, and ray tracing does not exist there.

Nothing is wrong with your graphics card. Restart the game (one instance at a time) and Radiante will start on Vulkan again.
screen.radiante.unsupported.title.init_f: Radiante: ray tracer failed to start
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.init:
Your graphics card supports ray tracing, but Radiante's renderer could not start this time. This usually happens when several Minecraft instances start at once, or when video memory is short.

Close the other instances and restart the game. If it keeps happening, the cause is in logs/latest.log.
screen.radiante.vulkan.title: Switched to Vulkan
screen.radiante.vulkan.message:
The game will use Vulkan the next time it starts, and Radiante can take over from there.

Restart the game to try it.
options.radiante.biome_ambiance.tooltip: Each biome's own air and water, kept subtle: warm dust over deserts, a green murk over swamps, a cold bright mist over snow, red, teal and ash in the Nether, violet in the End; under water, clear and bright by a beach, dark and close in the deep ocean. Fades from one biome to the next, stays out of caves, and works with or without Volumetric Fog. A Bedrock RTX pack's own values are used where it has them; biomes from mods get theirs worked out automatically.
options.radiante.block_light_sampling.to: Surfaces aim a shadow ray at a nearby light block (torch, lava, lamp) instead of waiting for a random bounce to find it. Much less noise at night and in caves, for a small cost. Needs Block Emission.
options.radiante.sun_path.tooltip: The way the sun and moon cross the sky. Vanilla: straight overhead from east to west. Tilted: the path leans ten degrees south, so noon shadows are not straight down. Custom: set in Sun & Moon Path under the Advanced settings, which also turn the path, turn the sun and moon squares and give the moon a path of its own.
options.radiante.sun_path_tilt.tooltip: How far the sun's path leans from straight overhead. Positive leans it south, negative north; the sun still rises and sets at the same times. Shadows, clouds, fog and water follow it.
options.radiante.sun_path_azimuth.toolti: Turns the sun's path around the sky. Positive turns it clockwise seen from above, moving sunrise from the east towards the south. Shadows, clouds, fog and water follow it.
options.radiante.sun_sprite_rotation.too: Turns the sun's square around its own centre. Only how it looks; the light is the same.
options.radiante.moon_follows_sun.toolti: The moon crosses the sky on the sun's path, opposite the sun, as in vanilla. Off, the moon's path has a tilt and rotation of its own; it still rises as the sun sets.
options.radiante.moon_path_tilt.tooltip: How far the moon's path leans from straight overhead. Positive leans it south, negative north. Moonlit shadows follow it.
options.radiante.moon_path_azimuth.toolt: Turns the moon's path around the sky. Positive turns it clockwise seen from above, moving moonrise from the east towards the south.
options.radiante.moon_sprite_rotation.to: Turns the moon's square around its own centre. Only how it looks; the light is the same.
options.radiante.vanilla_celestial_orien: Keep the sun and moon squares lined up with their path like vanilla, instead of turning as they cross the sky.
options.radiante.first_person_shadow.too: Draw the player for shadows and reflections while the camera is in first person. Minecraft itself skips the player then, so without this you cast no shadow and do not appear in water or glass.
options.radiante.held_item_light.tooltip: A torch, lantern or other light source held in either hand lights up its surroundings.
options.radiante.day_brightness.tooltip: Brightness of sunlight and the daytime sky. 100% is the shader pack's own.
options.radiante.night_brightness.toolti: Brightness of moonlight and the night sky. 100% is the shader pack's own.
options.radiante.quality.tooltip: Sets the settings that cost the most frame time at once: DLSS mode, block light sampling, volumetric fog, clouds and render distance. Changing any of them afterwards shows Custom.
options.radiante.reset_defaults.tooltip: Puts every setting on this screen back to its default.
options.radiante.emission_brightness.too: Brightness of blocks that give off light (torches, lava, glowstone...).
options.radiante.held_light_brightness.t: Brightness of what you hold in your hand: a torch, lantern or lava bucket, both its own glow and the light it casts around you.
options.radiante.block_outline.tooltip: The outline around the block under the crosshair.
options.radiante.parallax_transparent_ed: With resource packs that carve their textures (parallax), the carved part at the outer edges of a block is see-through, as if really cut away. Off, those edges show the border's colour.
options.radiante.volumetric_fog_strength: How thick the air that shows sunbeams and light shafts is. 100% is the tuned look; lower it if the fog feels too heavy. No effect on performance.
options.radiante.hdr_output.tooltip: Shows the traced world in HDR on an HDR display: sunlight, lava, lamps and reflections go brighter than white. Needs HDR turned on in Windows. Takes effect after restarting the game.
options.radiante.hdr_output.tooltip_pend: On, but not running: restart the game, and check that HDR is turned on in the Windows display settings.
options.radiante.hdr_peak.tooltip: The brightest your display can show, in nits (see its specifications, or Windows HDR Calibration). Highlights are fitted under this.
options.radiante.hdr_paper_white.tooltip: How bright menus, text and the world's ordinary surfaces are, in nits. Raise it in a bright room, lower it in a dark one.
options.radiante.hdr_debug_view.tooltip: Tints blue everything shown in SDR (menus, text). What keeps its normal colour is the world in HDR.
options.radiante.ray_bounces.tooltip: How many times light bounces off surfaces (1-128). Fewer is much faster (4 to 2: about +50% fps). Above 4 costs a lot and is meant for powerful GPUs; past 8 the picture barely changes and the high values are there to experiment with; mirrors and clear glass get extra bounces on their own.
options.radiante.parallax.tooltip: Depth on resource pack textures that have height maps (bricks, stones stand out). Off: flat and faster. No effect without such a pack.
options.radiante.bedrock_materials.toolt: Bedrock RTX packs (.mcpack): metal, roughness and shine read straight from the pack's MER maps at full detail, as Bedrock does, instead of from the converted copy (ore specks and metal edges keep their reflections). No effect on Java packs.
Samples per ray for the volumetric fog. Lower is faster and a little noisier; 32 costs about 30% more than 16.
options.radiante.atmosphere_style.toolti: Bedrock: the sky and sunlight colours of Bedrock RTX, read from a Bedrock install on this PC (or radiante/bedrock/sky.png and look_up_tables.png). Java: Radiante's own scattered sky. Without the Bedrock files the Java sky is used.
options.radiante.advanced.tooltip: Shows every setting of the render pipeline and shader pack under the usual ones, in groups you can fold open. Turning it off only hides them: their values stay in effect.
options.radiante.picture_style.tooltip: Natural: physically based light and colour. Bedrock: tuned to match Bedrock RTX (more saturated, brighter shade and bounced light). Vivid: stronger contrast and colour.
options.radiante.tone_method.tooltip: How bright light is fitted to the screen. PBR Neutral keeps colours true; ACES is filmic with more contrast; Reinhard is soft and flat.
options.radiante.tunable.saturation.tool: How colourful the image is. 100% is unchanged.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_adapta: How far the exposure adapts to what you look at. Lower keeps dark rooms dark and daylight bright, as in Bedrock; 100% always evens the image out.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_bias.t: Overall brightness of the image, in photographic stops.
options.radiante.tunable.bounce_light.to: How much light carries on after bouncing off surfaces. Higher fills rooms from a single patch of sunlight, as Bedrock RTX does; 100% is physically based.
options.radiante.tunable.sky_light.toolt: How strongly the open sky lights the world. Higher brightens shade under buildings and trees.
options.radiante.tunable.glass_reflectio: How much of the sky windows show on top of what is behind them. 0% is perfectly clear glass.
options.radiante.tunable.water_texture.t: How much of the resource pack's water texture shows over the surface, as Bedrock RTX draws it. 0% is clear, see-through water without the pattern.
options.radiante.tunable.texture_contras: How deep and contrasted block and entity colors look under the light. 100% matches Bedrock RTX; lower gives the paler, flatter look of earlier versions.
options.radiante.renderer_profile.toolti: Bedrock RTX (Enhanced): the look of Bedrock RTX, rebuilt after the real renderer: a pack's materials exactly as authored, Bedrock's sky and sunlight, its exposure and tone mapping, its glass and water (reflections, tint, caustics, the view under water), its fog and bloom. On top of that, a few things that look better than Bedrock RTX: light blocks whose pack gives them little glow (a redstone torch, redstone ore) look lit by their own light, and the end portal glows. You can still change any setting: changing one that the profile sets turns it into Custom, which keeps everything as you left it. Pick Bedrock RTX (Enhanced) again to get its values back.
options.radiante.tunable.light_shafts.to: Beams of light through windows, skylights and leaves. Needs volumetric fog.
options.radiante.tunable.water_waves.too: How rough the water surface is. 0% is a flat, mirror-like surface.
options.radiante.tunable.water_density.t: How quickly the water fades out with distance, from the inside. Lower is clearer.
Shafts of sunlight through the water surface while under water.
options.radiante.apply.tooltip: Apply the changes now and keep the screen open.
options.radiante.undo.tooltip: Discard the changes made since the last Apply.
options.radiante.subtitle: Ray tracing
options.radiante.applying.detail: Compiling shaders. Progress is shown in the window title; this can take a moment.
options.radiante.upscaler_mode.tooltip: The resolution the world is traced at before FSR or XeSS scales it to the screen. Native traces every pixel; lower modes are much faster and softer. The Quality level sets it too. Custom lets you set the resolution yourself.
options.radiante.restart.hint: Takes effect after restarting the game.
options.radiante.restart.title: Restart required
options.radiante.restart.message: These changes take effect the next time the game starts:
options.radiante.rain_wetness.tooltip: Surfaces under open sky turn darker and glossy while it rains, and dry slowly after it stops.
options.radiante.entity_light_reach.tool: How far from you, in blocks, glowing dropped items and items in frames (glowstone, sea lanterns...) still light their surroundings. Further costs a little more when many are around.
options.radiante.cache_deep_bounces.tool: Past the first bounce, light is taken from the radiance cache instead of traced further, and bounced surfaces stop searching for block lights, as Bedrock RTX does. Much faster in places full of lights; bounced light can look slightly softer.
options.radiante.bedrock_one_bounce.tool: Like Bedrock RTX: only one bounce of light is traced everywhere, and the rest comes from the radiance cache where it lands. The biggest gain; indirect light in uncached spots is a little darker for a moment.
options.radiante.transparent_checkerboar: Water and glass trace either their reflection or their refraction per pixel, alternating in a checkerboard, instead of both: one ray per pixel instead of two, as Bedrock RTX does.
options.radiante.seamless_glass.tooltip: Hides the frame vanilla draws around every glass block, so a wall of glass looks like one big sheet instead of a grid of blocks.
options.radiante.rain_refraction.tooltip: Raindrops bend the view behind them like little lenses. Costs almost nothing.
options.radiante.cloud_shadows.tooltip: Volumetric clouds cast soft shadows on the ground as they drift over. Only with Volumetric clouds.
options.radiante.frame_generation_backen: Which frame generation to use. Auto picks DLSS where the GPU runs it and FSR otherwise. FSR works with any upscaler (DLSS included) but only doubles the frame rate.
options.radiante.restir.tooltip: Reuses the light each pixel picked from torches, lamps and other block lights over time and across neighbouring pixels. Much less noise in rooms lit by many lights, and it looks at fewer new lights per frame than without it. Needs Block Light Sampling.
options.radiante.ser.tooltip: NVIDIA RTX 40 and newer: the GPU regroups rays by what they hit before shading them, which usually gains frame rate in ray traced scenes. Has no effect on other GPUs. Experimental: water can look white with it on.
options.radiante.motion_blur.tooltip: Smears what moves across the screen along its motion, as a camera does. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.depth_of_field.tooltip: Keeps what you look at sharp and blurs what is much nearer or farther, focusing by itself on the centre of the screen. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.fog_style.tooltip: How the volumetric fog is made. Froxel: the air is cut into a 3D grid lit once per cell and kept over frames; sharper light shafts, block lights glow in the fog, and cheaper. Radiante: every pixel marches the air itself; follows each surface exactly but costs more.
options.radiante.volumetric_fog.tooltip: Ray marches the air like Bedrock RTX: sunlight and moonlight scatter in the biome fog and trees and terrain cast light shafts through it. Costs noticeably more GPU time than the plain haze.
options.radiante.reflex.tooltip: Low latency mode: holds the CPU back so each frame starts as late as the GPU allows, cutting input lag. NVIDIA GPUs only.
screen.radiante.download.dlss.title: NVIDIA DLSS
screen.radiante.download.dlss.message: Your NVIDIA GPU can use DLSS (upscaling, Ray Reconstruction and frame generation) for better performance and a cleaner image. It is downloaded from NVIDIA (about %s MB) and used from the next start. FSR keeps working meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.xess.title: Intel XeSS
screen.radiante.download.xess.message: Intel XeSS upscaling can be downloaded from Intel (about %s MB) and is used from the next start. FSR keeps working meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.finished: Done. Restart the game to use it.
screen.radiante.download.delete.message: Remove the downloaded files? You can download them again any time. Files in use are removed on the next start.
options.radiante.download.tooltip: Downloaded on request from NVIDIA or Intel. Click to download or delete.
options.radiante.download.leave_world: Leave the world first: installing or deleting an upscaler is done from the menus and needs a restart.
screen.radiante.download.restart.message: The change is ready. Radiante loads upscalers when the game starts, so the game has to be restarted now to avoid errors.
options.radiante.ray_tracing.tooltip: Switches between Radiante's ray traced renderer and Minecraft's own, at once, like the Toggle Ray Tracing key (unbound by default, set it in Controls). The world is rebuilt for the renderer that takes over.
options.radiante.chunk_building_auto.too: Automatic sizes chunk building to your CPU so it does not starve the game while chunks load. This CPU has %s threads: %s chunk threads, batches of %s, %s batches at once. Manual shows the three sliders.
message.radiante.showcase.usage: Radiante: /radiante showcase (build here), /radiante showcase 1-14 (go to a room), /radiante showcase blocks (every block, by category), /radiante showcase clear, /radiante biome [next|back|list|<name>] (visit each biome)
message.radiante.showcase.singleplayer: Radiante: the showcase can only be built in a singleplayer world.
message.radiante.showcase.built: Radiante: showcase built, heading east. Each room has a sign saying what to check. /radiante showcase 1-14 jumps to a room.
message.radiante.showcase.none: Radiante: no showcase built in this session. Stand where it should start and run /radiante showcase.
message.radiante.showcase.blocks: Radiante: every block laid out heading east, one category per group of rows, each started by a sign.
message.radiante.biome.at: Radiante: %s (%s/%s) at %s %s %s. /radiante biome for the next one, /radiante biome back for the previous.
message.radiante.biome.not_found: Radiante: %s (%s/%s) not found within 6400 blocks. /radiante biome skips to the next.
message.radiante.biome.unknown: Radiante: no biome called %s in this dimension. /radiante biome list shows them.
How quickly the exposure follows when you walk from the dark into the light or back. Lower lets you see your eyes adjust for a moment, as in Bedrock; 100% is close to instant.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_strength.to: How strongly what is out of focus blurs. Needs Depth of Field.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_range.toolt: How much around what you look at stays sharp. Lower blurs sooner, for a close-up look. Needs Depth of Field.
options.radiante.dof_auto_focus.tooltip: Depth of Field focuses on whatever is at the centre of the screen. Off keeps the focus at Focus Distance, for screenshots. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_focus_dista: How far away the image is sharp when Auto Focus is off.
options.radiante.tunable.motion_blur_str: How long the smear of Motion Blur is.
options.radiante.tunable.fsr_sharpness.t: How much FSR sharpens the upscaled image. Higher is crisper but can show halos on edges.
options.radiante.tunable.low_light_boost: How much the exposure may brighten a dark scene. Higher lets you see more in caves and at night; lower keeps the dark dark.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_day.to: How bright the picture is kept by day, against what the light meter alone would make it. Lower is darker.
How bright the picture is kept at night, against what the light meter alone would make it. Lower is darker.
options.radiante.tunable.day_low_light_l: How far the exposure may open by day in a dark place. Low keeps closed rooms dark; high brightens rooms lit only through a window.
options.radiante.tunable.mirror_smoothne: Metals at least this smooth are drawn as clean, sharp mirrors. 0% turns this off.
How much of the sky volumetric clouds cover.
options.radiante.tunable.cloud_quality.t: Steps taken through volumetric clouds per ray. Higher is smoother and costs frame rate.
options.radiante.tunable.fog_distance.to: How far volumetric fog and light shafts reach, in blocks.
options.radiante.star_altitude.tooltip: How much clearer the stars get the higher you are: at 100% they are twice as bright from a mountain top (around Y 190) as from sea level, where less air lies over you. 0% keeps them the same everywhere. With Biome Ambiance on, the biome's air counts too: sharper over deserts, peaks and the open sea, dimmer in the haze of a swamp or a jungle.
options.radiante.tunable.stars.tooltip: How many stars the night sky has.
options.radiante.render_scale.tooltip: The share of the screen resolution the world is traced at before the upscaler scales it up, by hand. Lower is faster and softer. Only in the Custom upscaling mode; choosing a Quality level or another mode leaves it. Below 33% no upscaler is designed to work: expect a very blurry, flickering image. DLSS never goes under 240 pixels of height.
screen.radiante.download.dlss.switch: DLSS is installed and ready. Switch to the DLSS pipeline now? It is the recommended one for your NVIDIA GPU: better performance and a cleaner image. You can change it later in the Radiante settings.
screen.radiante.download.xess.switch: XeSS is installed and ready. Switch to the XeSS pipeline now? You can change it later in the Radiante settings.
options.radiante.render_scale.limited.to: The share of the screen resolution the world is traced at before the upscaler scales it up. Lower is faster and softer. FSR and XeSS are designed for 33% at the lowest, which is the minimum here; 50% to 67% is the recommended range. Only in the Custom mode.
options.radiante.output_resolution.toolt: The size the world is rendered and upscaled to before a final FSR 1 upscale fills the window, like the render resolution setting of many games. The HUD, menus and text stay sharp at the window's resolution. On a large screen (4K) this is the biggest saving there is: the tracer, the denoiser and the upscaler all work for the smaller picture. Sizes at or above the window's are not offered. Native renders at the window's size.
options.radiante.output_scale.tooltip: The share of the window's size the world is rendered at with the Custom output resolution, with the size that comes out. Lower is faster and softer; the HUD, menus and text stay at the window's resolution either way.
How many reflections inside reflections are traced on top of Light Bounces: mirrors facing each other, glass behind glass, water seen in a mirror. Only surfaces that are almost perfectly smooth count, so it needs a PBR resource pack; water and glass always count. Costs frame rate only where mirrors face each other.
options.radiante.share.tooltip: Your saved looks: keep the current one, switch between them with a click, import a code someone sent you or copy one to share.
screen.radiante.share.title: Presets
screen.radiante.share.message: A look: lighting, sky, fog, water, tone and camera effects. Upscaler, frame generation and HDR stay as they are.
screen.radiante.share.copied: Code copied. Paste it wherever you want to share it.
screen.radiante.share.invalid: The clipboard does not hold a Radiante code.
screen.radiante.share.skipped: Imported. %s settings in the code are not known to this version and are skipped.
options.radiante.advanced.more: %s more in Advanced (turn it on below)
options.radiante.mod_overlays.tooltip: Lets other mods draw into the traced world: Litematica schematics and selection boxes, MiniHUD shapes, waypoint beams, guides and markers. They are drawn Minecraft's way, on top of the traced picture, and are hidden behind the traced world as they should be. Turn it off if a mod draws something wrong over the world.
options.radiante.text_backgrounds.toolti: Draws the translucent plate behind text displays - leaderboards, holograms and server signs - as Minecraft does, so the text is easier to read. Off shows only the letters.
screen.radiante.share.empty: No presets yet. Save your current look, or import a code from the clipboard.
screen.radiante.share.name: Name
screen.radiante.share.imported: Imported as %s. Pick Apply to use it.
screen.radiante.share.need_name: Type the new name in the box first.
screen.radiante.share.full: The preset could not be kept.
screen.radiante.share.name.hint: Name for the preset you save, import or rename...
screen.radiante.share.save.tooltip: Adds the look the game has now to the list, under the name typed above.
screen.radiante.share.paste.tooltip: Adds a preset from a code someone shared. Copy the code first; it is not applied until you pick Apply.
screen.radiante.share.apply.tooltip: Switches to the picked preset. The shaders are compiled again when the preset changes how they are built. Clicking a preset twice does the same.
screen.radiante.share.copy.tooltip: Copies the picked preset as a code, to send to someone.
screen.radiante.share.rename.tooltip: Gives the picked preset the name typed above.
screen.radiante.share.delete.tooltip: Removes the picked preset from the list. Your current look is not changed.
screen.radiante.share.hint.in_use: This is the look the game has now.
screen.radiante.share.hint.apply: Pick Apply, or click it again, to switch to it.
screen.radiante.share.hint.pick: Pick a preset to see it here.
options.radiante.blocked.needs: No effect right now: turn on %s first.
options.radiante.blocked.needs_value: No effect right now: needs %s set to %s.
options.radiante.blocked.overridden: No effect right now: %s takes its place.
options.radiante.blocked.profile: Set by the Bedrock RTX (Enhanced) renderer profile. Change it to turn the profile into Custom.
options.radiante.blocked.ray_tracing: No effect while Ray Tracing is off.
options.radiante.preset.tooltip: What finishes the traced picture: the denoiser and the upscaler. DLSS Ray Reconstruction on NVIDIA RTX cards; NRD with FSR or XeSS on any GPU. DLSS and XeSS are downloaded the first time you pick them.
options.radiante.debug_logging.tooltip: Writes extra details about the renderer to the game log, for bug reports. Changes nothing in the picture.
render_pipeline.module.ray_tracing.attri: Which glass Seamless Glass joins into one sheet: blocks and panes, only blocks, or only panes.
options.radiante.notice.profile: Set by the %1$s profile. Changing it turns the profile into Custom; pick %1$s again to restore it.
options.radiante.notice.custom_profile: Custom: the Bedrock RTX (Enhanced) profile with settings changed by hand. Nothing is written over; pick the profile again to put its values back.
options.radiante.blocked.bedrock_fog: No effect right now: Bedrock's fog does not use it. It works with the Radiante profile, or with Bedrock Volumetric Fog turned off under Advanced.
